assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 biology moved from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) to approved incretin therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits. Few discoveries in physiology have combined mechanistic clarity with such large and measurable clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst on native GLP-1 physiology and secretion, Drucker on intestinotropic and receptor biology and translation, and Mojsov on the active peptide form and its synthesis form a defensible three-person core. Knudsen's industrial design of long-acting analogues is also decisive for the therapy but would crowd the three-person limit; Mojsov's credit relative to others is contested.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is replicated in many laboratories and the clinical effect is confirmed in large randomized trials; the field is mature, and recognition is timely as therapeutic impact is now unmistakable.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the peptide discovery, the receptor biology and the pharmaceutical development, including Mojsov's disputed role and Knudsen's exclusion.
Long-term safety and durability data are still accumulating, though this does not undermine the core discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated microbial channelrhodopsins used to control defined cell types with millisecond precision created a general experimental method that reshaped neuroscience and physiology, enabling causal circuit dissection across many species.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsin as a light-gated channel, while Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control and drove broad adoption; Bamberg and Miesenboeck also made early contributions. Six credited names cannot all be accommodated, so any trio omits genuinely important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Technique has been independently validated for over fifteen years in thousands of studies; clinical translation (vision restoration) is early, but the tool value is well established, so recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Credit split between the discovery of the protein, the first neuronal demonstration and the broader toolkit.
Possible view that this is a method rather than a physiological discovery, though methods have been recognized before.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed to tumour antigens produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemias and lymphomas and established a new class of living therapeutics. The principle is original, clear and clinically validated.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain developed and clinically validated costimulation-enhanced CD19 CAR-T cells, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified lymphocytes in patients. Eshhar's original chimeric receptor concept is not among the credited names, which weakens the fairness of any configuration drawn only from this list.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products, multi-year remissions and independent confirmations show maturity; solid tumour efficacy remains limited, but this does not undermine the core discovery.
uncertainties: Absence of the originator of the chimeric receptor concept among credited names.
Toxicity, relapse and limited solid-tumour success.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mechanistic dissection of SMN2 exon 7 splicing led to splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides, with nusinersen changing the natural history of spinal muscular atrophy. It is a clear bridge from RNA processing basic science to a transformative therapy for a fatal childhood disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and identified the target sequence, while Bennett led antisense chemistry and development with Ionis; the pair is a compact and coherent configuration. Others (e.g., academic groups in the field) may have claims not captured in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approval since 2016 and a decade of real-world data confirm benefit; the antisense platform is now broadly validated, so recognition is timely though the oligonucleotide field may still be considered maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the prize as mainly an RNA therapeutics platform rather than a single discovery.
Competing contributions from other splicing and antisense laboratories are not evident from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particles from recombinant L1 capsid protein elicit strong protective immunity and have been shown to prevent persistent HPV infection, precancerous lesions and increasingly invasive cervical cancer, giving a major population-level cancer prevention tool.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller established L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity, and Frazer with the late Jian Zhou developed the VLP approach in parallel; the supplied credited names omit Zhou, who is deceased and ineligible. The three credited names are a plausible set.
assessment.maturity: Vaccines are licensed worldwide with strong effectiveness data in real-world populations; population-level cancer reduction is now emerging, making the timing good.
uncertainties: Overlap with previous recognition of HPV-cancer discoveries and the role of commercial development.
Priority between Frazer/Zhou and the NIH group.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and PERK/ATF6 arms that govern proteostasis, and is relevant to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. It is a conceptually original and widely confirmed discovery.
assessment.attribution: Mori identified the UPR transcriptional response and Walter discovered IRE1 and the unconventional mRNA splicing mechanism; the two-person configuration is clean and widely accepted, though other contributors (e.g., Ron, Kaufman) may be considered.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of independent confirmation; clinical translation of UPR modulation is still limited, but the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Relatively limited direct therapeutic output so far.
Possible claims of other investigators on PERK/ATF6 arms.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and of mTOR complexes as central regulators of growth, nutrient sensing and metabolism established a fundamental organizing principle with implications for cancer, ageing, diabetes and immunology.
assessment.attribution: Hall's identification of TOR in yeast is the foundational discovery; Sabatini contributed the mammalian mTOR identification, mTORC1/2 definition and nutrient-sensing pathways. Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin is relevant but is a separate chemical-biology contribution; Brown and Sabatini's mTOR cloning also involved others not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed and now textbook; clinical implications (rapalogs, transplant, oncology) are established, though lifespan-related claims remain mixed. Sabatini's recent professional controversies could complicate fairness for some members.
uncertainties: Whether to include Schreiber and how to apportion credit among Hall, Sabatini and earlier mTOR cloners.
Non-scientific considerations affecting one potential laureate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and subsequent BCR-ABL inhibitors demonstrated that targeting a driver kinase can convert a fatal leukaemia into a manageable chronic condition, validating the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the compound programme, Druker brought it to clinical proof of concept, and Sawyers identified resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors; the trio is coherent. Rowley, Witte and others who defined BCR-ABL are not in the credited names, so recognition may be seen as incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of survival data and extensive confirmation make maturity very strong; timing could be seen as late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether upstream discoverers of the Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL would be needed for a fair prize.
